concept FolderBrowserConcept:
    pitch:
        A folder picker drawn by the application itself rather than the
        platform's native dialog, so it looks and behaves the same everywhere
        and sits inside whatever panel needs it.

    shape: {FolderBrowserShape}

shape FolderBrowserShape:
    description:
        A title saying what the folder is being chosen for, a bar for getting
        around, the folders in the current folder, and buttons to choose or
        cancel along the bottom. It starts in whatever folder it is given, or
        the user's home folder when that doesn't exist.

    navigation:
        The bar holds an up button, disabled at the top of the file system, and
        a home button, each with a tooltip, then the current folder's path as a
        breadcrumb, where clicking any folder along it goes straight there. At
        the right end, a "Show hidden" checkbox, off by default, shows the
        folders whose names start with a dot. Its label is shown in full, never
        cut off below its baseline.

    folders:
        The current folder's folders, never its files, each a row with a folder
        icon and its name, sorted by name ignoring case, with a
        @{ScrollbarScope}. Clicking a row selects it, highlighted; clicking
        it twice goes into it. A folder with no folders in it reads
        "No folders here", and one that can't be read says why in place of the
        list. Going to another folder clears the selection and scrolls back to
        the top.

    newFolder:
        The bar holds a "New Folder" button with a folder-plus icon, after the
        home button, whose tooltip says it creates a folder in the current one.
        Pressing it opens a row at the top of the list, above the folders: a
        folder icon, a name field with focus, a "Create" button, and a cancel
        button. <Enter> in the field creates the folder, as does Create; the
        cancel button, or <Escape> in the field, closes the row without creating
        anything, and <Escape> there doesn't close whatever the browser sits in.
        Going to another folder closes the row too.

        The name can't be empty, contain a slash or backslash, be "." or "..",
        or be the name of something already in the current folder; while it is
        one of those, once something has been typed, the row says why beneath
        the field and Create is disabled. A folder that can't be created says
        why the same way, and the row stays open.

        Once created, the row closes and the new folder is listed in its place
        among the others, selected and scrolled into view, so pressing Choose
        chooses it straight away.

    keyboard:
        overview:
            The browser can be used entirely from the keyboard, the way a
            platform's own file dialog can. It takes focus when it opens, on its
            list of folders, and the selected folder is always scrolled into
            view. <Tab> and <Shift+Tab> move between its controls: the bar's
            buttons, the breadcrumb, the checkbox, the list, and the footer's
            buttons. The keys below work wherever focus is in the browser,
            except while typing a new folder's name, where the name field has
            the keys.

        movingTheSelection:
            <Down> selects the next folder and <Up> the previous one; with
            nothing selected, <Down> selects the first and <Up> the last.
            Neither goes past the ends. <Home> selects the first folder and
            <End> the last. <Page Down> and <Page Up> move ten folders at a
            time, stopping at the ends.

        typeToSelect:
            Typing letters, digits, or other characters selects the first folder
            whose name starts with what has been typed, ignoring case. What is
            typed builds up while the keys come less than a second apart, and
            starts afresh after a longer pause. Typing that matches no folder
            leaves the selection where it is.

        going:
            <Enter> or <Right> goes into the selected folder. <Backspace>,
            <Left>, or <Alt+Up> (<Cmd+Up> on macOS) goes up to the folder
            holding the current one, and selects the folder just left, so going
            in and back out returns to where it was. <Alt+Home> (<Cmd+Shift+H>
            on macOS) goes to the home folder.

        choosingAndCancelling:
            <Ctrl+Enter> (<Cmd+Enter> on macOS) chooses, as the Choose button
            does. <Enter> with no folder selected chooses the current folder.
            <Escape> leaves without choosing, as Cancel does, once there is no
            new folder row open to close first.

        otherCommands:
            <Ctrl+H> (<Cmd+Shift+.> on macOS) switches Show hidden, keeping the
            selected folder selected when it is still listed. <Ctrl+Shift+N>
            (<Cmd+Shift+N> on macOS) opens the new folder row. Each button's
            tooltip gives its shortcut.

    choosing:
        The footer shows the folder that will be chosen: the selected folder, or
        the current folder when none is selected. "Choose" chooses it and
        "Cancel" leaves without choosing.

# The Piton Language

Piton is a declarative, whitespace-structured language for describing systems in
a mix of prose and structure. It has no runtime; a Piton program compiles to
data or, through a framework, to documents.

## Syntax

```piton
// A comment. Comments are line-only.
myVariable: 42                       // a number
myString: Strings are unquoted       // a string
myQuoted: "false"                    // quoting forces a string
myTyped:: string:: number: 42        // constraints, first match wins

myList:
    - one
    - two
myInlineList: [one, two, three]

myDictionary:
    nested:
        deep: value

computed: {1 + 2}                    // `{ }` evaluates; bare text does not
interpolated: Hello, ${myString}

anchor Base:
    name: Base
    summary: This is ${this.name}  // `this` pins to Base

anchor Child extends Base:
    name: Child
    detail: This is ${self.name}   // `self` follows the child
    summary: ${super.summary} and more

abstract anchor Shape as shape:      // `as` registers a keyword
    description:: string

shape Concrete:                      // same as `extends Shape`
    description: Implemented

from ./other import Thing, Other Alias
from ./other export *
use ./keywords
export anchor Published:
    value: 1
```

## Reserved words

`anchor`, `abstract`, `extends`, `as`, `export`, `from`, `import`, `use`, `this`, `self`, `super`, `true`, `false`, `null`

## Types

28:anchor Base:
29:    name: Base
30:    summary: This is ${this.name}  // `this` pins to Base
32:anchor Child extends Base:
40:shape Concrete:                      // same as `extends Shape`

72:  wins over its bases; a declaring keyword is the left-most base.

        breadcrumb, where clicking any folder along it goes straight there. At
        the right end, a "Show hidden" checkbox, off by default, shows the
        entries whose names start with a dot. Its label is shown in full, never
        cut off below its baseline.

content.text:
The Open Project button now uses the app's own browser instead of the system file dialog. The folder browser has become a general `FsBrowser`, which a folder browser and a new file browser both build on. All tests pass (172, 1 ignored); I haven't tried the picker in the running app.

**Spec:**
- **`FsBrowserScope`** (`spec/ui/components/fs-browser/index.pi`): everything the browsers share:
  - the title, the up/home/breadcrumb bar and "Show hidden";
  - the entry list, with folders first, then files;
  - the New Folder row and all the keyboard behaviour;
  - the footer with Cancel and Choose, which is disabled when there's nothing to choose.
- **`FolderBrowserScope`** extends it:
  - **What's listed:** only folders; "No folders here" when empty.
  - **What Choose picks:** the selected folder, or the current one if nothing is selected, so Choose is always enabled.
- **`FileBrowserScope`** (new) extends it:
  - **What's listed:** folders, plus only files with a given name, such as `piton.config.pi`.
  - **Opening and choosing:** double-clicking or pressing Enter on a file chooses it. Choose is disabled until a file is selected, and the footer says, for example, "Select a piton.config.pi".
- **Inheritance:** in Piton a child's section replaces the parent's section entirely. So the two browsers add their own `listed`, `opening` and `chosen` sections rather than rewriting the shared ones. The generated references show both the shared sections and each browser's additions.
- **`ProjectDirectoryScope`:** picking a project now opens a file browser in an inset panel, starting in the folder that holds the open project. Choosing a `piton.config.pi` opens its folder as the project.

**Code:**
- **`src/folder_browser.rs` → `src/fs_browser.rs`:** `FsBrowser` now takes a mode, folder or file with an optional required name. The choose and cancel events are renamed `ChoosePath` and `CancelBrowse`.
- **New Project:** its location picker is the same browser in folder mode.
- **Open Project:** the ribbon button and the palette's "Open Project…" now trigger an `OpenProject` action. The main window handles it by opening the file browser in the inset panel. The system dialog code in `project_directory.rs` is gone.

**Tests:**
- **File browser:** a new test checks the listing for each mode. It also checks Choose does nothing with only a folder selected, that Enter chooses a file, and that double-clicking goes into a folder and then chooses a file there.
- **Open Project:** a new main-window test clicks Open Project and checks no new window opens. It then checks only `piton.config.pi` is listed, not a neighbouring `notes.md`, and that double-clicking it opens the project and closes the panel.
- **Existing tests:** the keyboard and New Project browser tests pass, with one expectation updated for the new `choice()` return type.

`piton check`, `piton build check` and `piton build` ran cleanly, and the app builds with no warnings.
